open_points.subject: refusal reasons and proof-failure reasons
open_points.text: “refuses with one code of the closed set below and a bounded reason naming the first failing check”
open_points.question: What is the closed, exact set and payload shape of reason identifiers for `refused` results and ProofResult failures, including every ordered check named by the operations?
options: A distinct stable reason identifier for every check
One generic reason identifier plus bounded human-readable text
Operation-specific closed reason enumerations
open_points.default_guess: Use operation-specific stable reason identifiers, with bounded explanatory text kept separate.

open_points.subject: constant StoredValue schema in flows.compose_flow_version
open_points.text: “A constant's StoredValue takes the `value_schema` and class the composing agent declared with it (State 6, decision 5), never its target's”
open_points.question: Where does a constant's declared `value_schema` enter the operation, given that the Inputs mention only “constants with declared classes” and M16 names only target, value and declared class?
options: Each constant explicitly supplies its own schema
The constant uses its target port's schema
The schema is inferred from the literal value
open_points.default_guess: Require each constant to supply its own schema explicitly.

open_points.subject: capture_failed_execution refusal effects
open_points.text: “`runs` copies a spooled file into the content-addressed area only after every check of the capture has passed” / “the one exception is bytes a capture copied before `functions` refused the case”
open_points.question: Must all case-fit and fixture checks finish before any bytes are copied, or may `functions.add_captured_trial_case` refuse after copied bytes have been published and leave unreferenced bytes?
options: Preflight every check and copy nothing on refusal
Allow copied unreferenced bytes after a downstream refusal
Remove copied bytes when the downstream operation refuses
open_points.default_guess: Preflight every check and copy nothing on refusal.

open_points.subject: owner access to trial file fixtures
open_points.text: “The owner receives every value.” / “a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`” / “`read_spooled_file` takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue”
open_points.question: Can the owner retrieve the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?
options: Add an owner-only read for file-carriage StoredValues
Return fixture bytes inline in trial-case or repair-view answers
Owners receive only fixture metadata despite the earlier disclosure rule
open_points.default_guess: Allow an owner-only byte read for file-carriage StoredValues.

open_points.subject: agent view of EffectApproval.preview
open_points.text: “`preview`: what the owner saw — operation, target service, the built request and the input values” / “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value”
open_points.question: Exactly how is the built URL, query, headers and JSON or multipart body masked when it embeds personal-data inputs and an agent reads an approval record?
options: Replace every request component derived from personal data with digest and class
Omit the built request from an agent's approval view
Return the request description unchanged while masking only the separate input fields
open_points.default_guess: Mask every request component derived from personal data, not only the separately listed inputs.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request required-header checks
open_points.text: “a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed, then the credential, then input placement”
open_points.question: Where is `required_header_invalid` checked, and does it precede `plain_http_not_allowed` as A09 rule 6 requires?
options: Check repeated header, invalid header, plain HTTP, credential, then input placement
Check invalid headers during binding-current checking instead
Do not recheck invalid required headers at send time
open_points.default_guess: Check repeated header, then invalid header, then plain HTTP, credential and input placement.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file storage failures
open_points.text: “Errors: `refused` over a spool ceiling” / “a link found later makes that store call fail with nothing written”
open_points.question: What does `store.spool_file` return for a symbolic link, I/O failure, digest-publication failure or other non-ceiling store failure?
options: Return `internal_error` with nothing published
Return `refused`
Return a separate storage-failure result for the caller to conclude

open_points.subject: store.spool_file after an interrupted read attempt
open_points.text: “a `read` element without [a concluded record] is sent again” / “a completed file is never overwritten”
open_points.question: If a read response file was spooled but its NodeExecution was not committed, recovery reuses the same next attempt identity; what happens when the resend spools the same port and list index again, especially if its bytes differ?
options: Reuse the existing file only when its digest matches and fail otherwise
Keep both physical files and let the later record select one
Replace the unrecorded earlier file
Allocate a new attempt identity before resending
open_points.default_guess: Reuse it when the digest matches and return an internal consistency error when it differs.

open_points.subject: effects.operation_element_conclusion for skipped operation nodes
open_points.text: “Its conclusion: succeeded with outputs; failed with its status ... waiting with its reason ... or not reached”
open_points.question: What conclusion does this operation return for an operation node whose NodeExecution is `skipped_by_guard`, given that `runs` writes that record but reads operation-element conclusions through `effects`?
options: A distinct `skipped_by_guard` conclusion
Treat it as succeeded without outputs
Treat it as not reached
Let `runs` bypass this operation for records it wrote

open_points.subject: acting Actor recorded by nested operations
open_points.text: “Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27” / “the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record”
open_points.question: For each store change, which actor is actually recorded when an agent request triggers automatic work—particularly admission TrialExecutions and verdicts, automatic Activations, node executions, attempts and run advancement—and where is that actor stored when the State 1 model has no actor field?
options: Record the requesting actor for all nested work
Record `kernel` for automatic admission, activation and execution decisions, and the requester only for the initiating record
Add both initiating and acting actors
Pass an actor to store changes but persist it only on models that already name an actor
open_points.default_guess: Persist an acting actor on every action record, using `kernel` for automatic admission and activation and the request actor for request-driven advancement.

open_points.subject: record immutability versus lifecycle updates
open_points.text: “records are never edited (A01 rule 6)” / “a lifecycle change ... updates those fields of the entity's one record in place”
open_points.question: Does `store` update entity records such as bindings, approvals, grants, attempts and runs in place, or append immutable lifecycle records and derive their current state?
options: Update the permitted lifecycle fields in place
Append immutable transition records
Use in-place updates for some named entities and append transitions for others
open_points.default_guess: Update only the explicitly listed lifecycle fields in place; keep all other records and fields immutable.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.content_identity identity recipe
open_points.text: “One content record's meaning facts as State 1 names them for that record, or one value”
open_points.question: How does the operation know which identity recipe and order-free-list sorting rules apply, especially when it is called for a manifest capability digest, request digest, idempotency key, StoredValue or version identity?
options: The caller supplies an explicit identity kind
There is one generic canonical hash and callers pre-sort model-specific lists
The operation infers the recipe from the input object's shape
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit identity kind and apply only that kind's defined sorting recipe.

open_points.subject: trial execution actor for try versus admission
open_points.text: “Trying an implementation ... records one TrialExecution per case” / “Admission executes ... each as one TrialExecution”
open_points.question: How can a TrialExecution produced by an agent's `try_implementation` be distinguished from one produced automatically by admission, and which actor should it name?
options: Add an execution purpose and actor to TrialExecution
Record only the actor
Infer the source from surrounding verdict records
Do not distinguish them
open_points.default_guess: Record both the purpose (`try` or `admission`) and the acting actor.
